hints: A pre-order list of values alone is not enough to rebuild the tree. What extra marker makes the shape unambiguous?

Encode with a pre-order DFS that writes # for every null child. Decode with the same DFS. Keep a shared index into the token list: a number creates a node and then reads its left and right children, and # means null.

1. encode(n): if n is null, append '#'. Otherwise append n.val, then encode(left) and encode(right).
  2. Join the tokens with commas.
  3. decode: split on commas and set pos = 0.
  4. read(): take tokens[pos++]. If it is '#', return null.
  5. Otherwise make a node, set left = read() and right = read(), and return the node.

approaches.name: Optimal (pre-order with null markers)
approaches.idea: Every node and every null child becomes exactly one token, so one recursive pass encodes and one pass decodes. Use a StringBuilder to avoid O(n²) string building.

explain: For [4,-2,7,null,null,5], the DFS writes 4, then -2 and its two missing children (#,#), then 7, then 5 and its two nulls, then 7's missing right child. That gives 4,-2,#,#,7,5,#,#,#. Decoding 3,#,9,1,#,#,# reads 3, then # for its left, then 9 for its right. 9 reads 1 as its left (1 has two nulls) and # as its right. The result is [3,null,9,1]. Decoding works because the null markers tell the reader exactly where each subtree ends. Watch out for negative values: parse them with Integer.parseInt, not character by character.
recognize: When you need to turn a tree into text and back, think of a pre-order DFS with explicit null markers.
